Our approach is generalizable and can be extended to a wide range of similar magnetic systems that are available for rigorous experimental tests.
title: Superparamagnetism in an Interacting Nanomagnet Array: A Tale of Three Temperatures

abstract: Thanks to electron-electron ($e$-$e$) collisions conserving momentum, metallic electron fluids are viscous. Yet, this viscosity is rarely detectable in bulk transport. Here, we report on the canonical realization of the Gurzhi effect in an elemental three-dimensional metal: cadmium. Using focused ion beam microstructuring to tune the effective thickness, we detected a low-temperature size-dependent resistivity upturn in a finite window sandwiched between ballistic and diffusive regimes. Within this window, the electrical conductivity displays a simultaneous quadratic dependence on both sample size and temperature -- fingerprint of a hydrodynamic flow. This leads us to quantify the amplitude and the temperature dependence of kinematic and dynamic viscosity of the electron fluid. In cadmium, in contrast with graphene and $^3$He, the rate of momentum-conserving $e$-$e$ collisions is not set by the main Fermi energy, but by Lilliputian energy scales and inter-valley bottlenecks.
title: Hydrodynamics of the Viscous Electron Fluid in Cadmium

abstract: Critical quantum metrology exploits the dramatic growth of the quantum Fisher information near quantum phase transitions to enhance the precision of parameter estimation. This enhancement is commonly associated with a closing energy gap, which causes the characteristic timescales for adiabatic preparation or relaxation to diverge with increasing system size. As a consequence, the apparent growth of the quantum Fisher information largely reflects the increasing evolution time induced by critical slowing down rather than a genuine improvement in metrological performance, thereby limiting the practical usefulness of such protocols. Here we show that the relationship between energy gaps, quantum correlations, and achievable precision in interacting quantum systems can be far more subtle. In particular, quantum-enhanced sensitivity can also emerge when the energy gap increases, eliminating critical slowing down and enabling substantially faster relaxation dynamics. Although the corresponding quantum Fisher information may decrease due to the shorter evolution time, the resulting precision can nevertheless remain quantum-enhanced. Building on this insight, we introduce an anti-critical quantum metrology scheme in which quantum-enhanced precision arises while the energy gap grows. We illustrate this mechanism using the quantum Rabi model, thereby identifying a route to metrological advantage that avoids the slow dynamics associated with conventional criticality.
title: Mind the gap: Anti-critical quantum metrology

abstract: Quantum physics forbids cloning of a qubit. Therefore, a qubit is irreversibly lost upon loss of the information carrier. To mitigate this physical loss, it has been proposed to distribute the logical information across an entangled set of physical qubits, some of which can be lost. Previous experiments illustrated this concept, but failed to demonstrate a gain in the information-retrieval efficiency. Here we address this challenge with photons for which the total loss, from generation to detection, is below the loss-tolerance threshold of 50 % . Using two single-atom emitters in an optical cavity, we encode information into the photons of a graph state and observe an efficiency gain for retrieving quantum correlations between the atoms and the photons for single-qubit measurements in the Pauli X and Z bases. Although technical errors reduce the probability to obtain the result, we achieve average fidelities as high as ≳ 70 % without and ≳ 75 % with error detection, demonstrating entanglement between the atomic and encoded photonic qubits. Lowering the encoding errors is a next natural step toward loss-tolerant photonic quantum-information processing.
title: Loss-tolerant quantum correlations between atomic and photonic qubits

abstract: We give a classical algorithm to sample from the outcome distribution μ Ψ M of a POVM~ M applied to a coherent superposition~ $\ket{\Psi}=\sum_{j=0}^{\chi-1} c_j\ket{\psi_j}$ of~ χ pure states. It assumes one can (i) evaluate the relevant outcome densities and (ii) sample from the distribution~ μ ρ M of the incoherent mixture~ $\rho=\sum_{j=0}^{\chi-1} (|c_j|^2/\|c\|^2_2)\ket{\psi_j}\!\bra{\psi_j}$ . With~ O ( χ ∥ c ∥ 2 2 log 1 / δ ) samples from~ μ ρ M , it returns one sample from~ μ Ψ M with probability at least~ 1 − δ . This covers POVMs with finite, countable, and continuous sets of outcomes, giving e.g., an efficient classical weak simulation algorithm for Gaussian measurements on superpositions of N -mode Gaussian states.
title: From Born probabilities and mixtures to samples for coherent superpositions

abstract: Nonlinear driving of electron spin resonance (ESR) is key to frequency mixing and up-conversion processes involving spin dynamics. Here, we demonstrate second- and third-harmonic driving of a single spin in a pentacene molecule using a radio-frequency electric field in a scanning tunneling microscope. High harmonic resonances in the tunneling current appear when the system is driven at integer fractions of the Larmor frequency, reaching amplitudes up to 20% of the linear response. Unlike multi-photon high harmonic generation found in quantum dots, our results are explained by the time-dependent modulation of the tunneling barrier and spin-dependent tunneling, which introduce transport nonlinearities in the presence of spin-polarized currents. This work establishes spin torque mediated by electron transport as a novel mechanism in nonlinear ESR that is applicable to both molecules and quantum dots.
title: High-harmonic electrically driven spin resonance by quantum spin torques

abstract: Femtosecond laser processing of semiconductor wafers is driven by applications in the electronics and photonics industry. X-ray free-electron lasers are powerful probes for revealing the ultrafast dynamics of the induced changes. We present a novel technique that provides time and depth resolved snapshots of the strain field upon laser excitation of bulk crystalline Si. At fluences below the melting threshold, coherent shear waves were found to propagate from the laser-excited surface into the bulk. Simulations support a propagation speed of 5.8km/s, slower than the longitudinal speed of sound, 8.4km/s.
title: Coherent shear wave in crystalline Si upon subthreshold femtosecond laser-induced excitation

abstract: Characterizing noise in superconducting qubits is essential for improving coherence and gate performance. Conventional noise-sensing methods typically use the qubit itself as the sensor, which limits both accessible bandwidth and applicability during driven operation. Here, we measure qubit frequency noise by detecting the photon loss it induces in a coupled high-Q superconducting cavity. We use repeated midcircuit qubit measurements with postselection to separate this induced loss from intrinsic cavity decay. We validate the protocol using injected noise and show that the extracted loss scales as expected with the applied noise strength. We place an upper bound of $0.70\ifmmode\times\else\texttimes\fi{}{10}^{3}\text{ }\text{ }{\mathrm{rad}}^{2}/\mathrm{s}$ on the intrinsic qubit frequency-noise power spectral density at the cavity-qubit detuning of 508 MHz. The protocol opens access to a higher-frequency spectral window than standard qubit-based spectroscopy and may enable noise characterization during strong driving.
title: Qubit Noise Sensing via Induced Photon Loss in a Superconducting Cavity

abstract: Next-to-next-to-leading order (NNLO) QCD corrections to quarkonium production and decay are known to exhibit perturbative instabilities within non-relativistic QCD. We identify the origin of this problem and propose a simple remedy. Applying our approach to S-wave color-singlet quarkonium processes, we achieve substantially improved perturbative convergence and agreement with experimental data.
title: Soft contributions stabilize next-to-next-to-leading-order QCD corrections to quarkonium production and decay

abstract: Topological bound states in the continuum (TBICs) provide an unconventional route toward robust wave localization with ultrahigh quality factors. Existing realizations, however, generally rely on explicitly engineered topological structures. Here, we propose and experimentally demonstrate a fundamentally different mechanism for generating TBICs through double-mirror-symmetric stacking of trivial bulks. In our scheme, one mirror symmetry decouples the system into independent parity subspaces, while an additional mirror symmetry within each subspace enables topological boundary states. Their interplay allows localized topological modes to spectrally coexist with bulk continuum states of opposite parity without hybridization, simply by tuning interlayer couplings. Using acoustic metamaterials, we realize first- and higher-order TBICs in one- and two-dimensional systems, manifesting as bound edge and bound corner states in the continuum. Extending the stacking scheme from two to three dimensions further yields higher-order TBICs featuring hinge states. Our work opens new avenues for engineering topological wave localization in artificial materials.
title: Emergence of topological bound states in the continuum via stacking trivial bulks with double mirror symmetry

abstract: To prevent overclosing the Universe, stable domain walls must decay—a problem typically addressed by breaking the Peccei-Quinn symmetry with a bias term. In this Letter, we present a novel mechanism in which a helical primordial magnetic field provides a spatially inhomogeneous ChernSimons source that drives the axion field. We validate this mechanism through three-dimensional lattice simulations of the evolving domain-wall network, demonstrating its effcacy in inducing decay. Our quantitative analysis reveals that the correlation length of the primordial magnetic field is a crucial determinant of the decay rate of the network and the properties of the emitted axions and gravitational waves. In particular, the axion emitted from the decaying domain-wall network can contribute to the dark matter abundance, and the associated gravitational-wave signal lies in the frequency range probed by pulsar timing array experiments.
title: Solving the domain wall problem: Primordial magnetic fields as a dynamical solution

abstract: Moiré superlattices in twisted graphene host correlated quantum phases in which electron-phonon interactions are expected to play an important yet elusive role. A key microscopic question is whether phonons of different symmetries couple to distinct electronic excitations, and how such coupling varies across the spatially modulated moiré landscape. Here, using dual-gated nano-infrared spectroscopy, we resolve nearly degenerate optical phonons of different symmetries in bilayer and twisted bilayer graphene and disentangle their coupling to distinct electronic excitations. The symmetric phonon mode couples to interband electron-hole pair excitations across a displacement-field-induced bandgap, whereas the antisymmetric mode couples to intraband plasmonic excitations arising from carrier doping. Both interactions generate dressed phonons with distinct Fano resonances, revealing robust coherent phonon-electron interference under confined near-field excitation. Applying this symmetry-resolved spectroscopy to twisted bilayer graphene, we image electron-phonon coupling at the moiré length scale and reveal gate-tunable, stacking-dependent modulation of local Fano responses. Our results establish dual-gated infrared nano-spectroscopy as a powerful probe of symmetry-dependent electron-phonon interactions in moiré quantum materials.
title: Imaging symmetry-resolved electron-phonon coupling in graphene moiré superlattices

abstract: We report on the experimental investigation of the californium isotopes 253 , 254 Cf by laser spectroscopy of two different atomic transitions at the RISIKO mass separator at Mainz University. The experimental results were complemented by state-of-the-art atomic theory calculations enabling the extraction of field-shift factors and transition strengths of several atomic transitions in californium. This allowed the determination of changes in mean-square nuclear charge radii for the californium isotopic chain. The charge radii of the Cf isotopes follow a similar trend as in fermium and nobelium isotopes across the N = 152 shell gap, suggesting collective behavior in this region of deformed nuclei that masks nuclear single-particle effects. By extending the theoretical calculations to consider all relevant transitions, we explore the implications of our work for kilonova spectra. Neutral Cf shows emission lines inside the spectral range of ground-based telescopes as well as the James Webb Space Telescope in a time frame of few weeks after the neutron-star merger, provided the r-process produces at least mid-actinide elements.
title: Optical spectroscopy of 253 , 254 Cf near the N = 152 neutron shell: implications for kilonova spectra

abstract: Distributed quantum sensing exploits entangled states to estimate global functions of physical quantities with enhanced sensitivity beyond the standard quantum limit (SQL). In practice, however, unavoidable decoherence degrades quantum coherence and can lead to sensitivities lower than those of classical strategies. Here, we propose and experimentally demonstrate a noise-robust distributed quantum sensing protocol that employs local unitary operations to maintain enhancement beyond the SQL under dephasing. Using a four-photon Greenberger–Horne–Zeilinger state with the local Hadamard operations, we estimate the average of four phases distributed across four nodes via 7 km of optical fiber in a dephasing environment and observe enhancements from 1.72 ± 0.29 dB to 3.01±0.17 dB over the SQL. Our results establish a practical route to decoherence-resilient quantum sensor networks with currently available entangled resources.
title: Decoherence-resilient distributed quantum sensing beyond the standard quantum limit

abstract: We introduce a minimal model of a two-dimensional lattice that, upon spontaneous symmetry breaking, simultaneously develops altermagnetic order, a finite electric polarization, and a spin-polarized transport response, all of which are controlled by an external electric field. By coupling a dimerized altermagnet to an external electric field, we show that the three order parameters are not merely compatible but dynamically entangled, so that switching one (for instance, reversing the polarization with an electric field) necessarily reconfigures the other two. We show that this model offers a clear physical blueprint for designing next-generation spintronic logic and pure spin current memdevices that merge the ultrafast, stray-field-free advantages of compensated magnets with the low-power switching architectures of ferroelectrics.
title: Electrically switchable spintronics in a multiferroic altermagnet

abstract: Multi-frequency photonic information processing capability is one of the core features of modern nanophotonic chips. On-chip rainbow devices, separating spatially and localizing photonic states of different frequencies, play a key role in integrated information processing. Here, we demonstrate on-chip photonic rainbow localization in a mid-infrared silicon photonic crystal through strain-induced confinement of an isolated quasi-flat band. Projection of the structural deformation onto this non-degenerate band produces a scalar confining potential, while an orthogonal graded duty ratio spatially separates the localized resonances according to wavelength. This mechanism does not require Dirac-point degeneracy or Landau quantization. Meanwhile, the states of different frequencies are spatially separated along the direction of a graded duty-ratio-induced scalar potential. Experimentally, the on-chip rainbow phenomenon is directly observed by spatially resolved far-field reflectance spectroscopy, covering a wide band in mid-infrared wavelength range. Our work opens new avenues for realizing photonic rainbow and for practically harnessing synthetic gauge fields, entailing broad implications for integrated photonic systems, including steerable light transport and wavelength-division multiplexing.
title: On-chip rainbow localization from synthetic photonic gauge fields

abstract: Altermagnets are characterized by anisotropic band/spin splittings in momentum space, dictated by their spin-space group symmetries. However, the real-space modulations of altermagnetism are often neglected and have not been explored experimentally. Here we combine neutron diffraction, angle-resolved photoemission spectroscopy (ARPES), spin-resolved ARPES and density functional theory to demonstrate that Cs$_{1-δ}$V$_2$Te$_2$O realizes a spatially modulated form of altermagnetism, i.e., hidden altermagnetism. Such a state in Cs$_{1-δ}$V$_2$Te$_2$O results from its G-type antiferromagnetism and two-dimensional electronic states, allowing for the development of spatially alternating altermagnetic layers, whose local spin polarizations are directly verified by spin-resolved ARPES measurements. Our experimental discovery of hidden altermagnetism broadens the scope of unconventional magnetism and opens routes to exploring emergent phenomena from real-space modulations of altermagnetic order.
title: Evidence for hidden altermagnetism in Cs 1 − δ V 2 Te 2 O

abstract: We investigate superconductivity emerging in the photodoped Mott insulating Hubbard model using steady-state dynamical mean-field theory implemented on the real-frequency axis. By employing high-order strong-coupling impurity solvers, we obtain the nonequilibrium phase diagram for photoinduced η -pairing superconductivity with a remarkably high effective critical temperature. We further identify a superconducting gap in the momentum-resolved spectral function and optical conductivity, providing spectroscopic signatures accessible to experiments. Our results highlight a route to a controllable form of high-temperature superconductivity in nonequilibrium strongly correlated systems, fundamentally distinct from the equilibrium s -wave pairing state in the attractive Hubbard model or cuprate-like d -wave superconductors.
title: High-temperature η -pairing superconductivity in the photodoped Hubbard model

abstract: Turbulence is commonly regarded as the ultimate state of disorder in which coherent structures do not persist in time averages. Here, we show that fully developed electrohydrodynamic turbulence in nematic liquid crystals instead supports a robust, system-spanning mean flow. Using high-speed imaging and particle tracking, we uncover a persistent large-scale vortex that emerges spontaneously from the dynamic scattering mode-2, a turbulent state studied for over five decades. This mean flow survives temporal averaging and reflects genuine material transport rather than apparent motion of orientational patterns. Three-dimensional nematohydrodynamic simulations reproduce the observed flow and reveal a Poiseuille-like velocity profile with vanishing interfacial shear stress, while two-dimensional modeling captures the coarsening dynamics leading to vortex selection. The emergence of a zero-wave-number flow directly from fully developed turbulence contrasts sharply with previously studied active and classical turbulent systems, where large-scale organization typically arises at finite wavelengths or requires external forcing.
title: Spontaneous Mean Flow Emerging from Electrohydrodynamic Turbulence in Nematic Liquid Crystals

abstract: Complex numbers are central to the standard formulation of quantum theory, but whether they are fundamentally necessary remains unsettled. Familiar real formulations reproduce quantum predictions but fail to be representation-local: local physical operations need not correspond to local entities in the mathematical representation. Here we show that representation-local formulations based solely on real numbers nevertheless exist. Our construction is based on the observation that not every structural feature of finite-dimensional density-matrix quantum theory over the complex numbers need be retained in a real formulation. Specifically, we reconsider two features inherited from the complex formalism: the use of the Kronecker product as the system-combination rule and the representation of states and effects by positive semidefinite matrices. Relaxing only one of these assumptions at a time, we first obtain a representation-local real quantum theory with a modified combination rule that closely parallels the conventional complex formulation. We then show that even with the usual Kronecker-product rule a representation-local real formulation exists, provided states and effects are not required to be positive.
title: Locality of quantum theory does not require complex numbers

abstract: The threshold at which density-limiting plasma instabilities occur in tokamak fusion reactors is not well understood. Here, we present the first large-scale empirical evidence of a common collisionality threshold present across multiple devices and confinement regimes. Machine-learning-guided analysis of a diverse experimental database identifies a scaling in edge effective collisionality ( ν * ) that bears resemblance to the widely utilized Greenwald limit but yields a substantially lower false positive rate. This threshold decreases with dimensionless pressure ( β ), consistent with theoretical expectations for enhanced transport from electromagnetic effects on resistive ballooning mode turbulence. These results suggest that future burning plasma devices such as ITER and ARC could potentially achieve higher density, and thus fusion power, than previously expected.
title: Collisionality scaling of the tokamak density limit

abstract: Unraveling the microscopic mechanisms governing the coupling between interfacial friction and sliding ferroelectricity is pivotal for advancing ultra-low-friction tribology and high-speed nonvolatile memory technologies. Here, we introduce ΔW, defined as the variation in orbital weight within a physically motivated energy window (~0.1 eV) for the uppermost occupied states bounded by the Debye energy scale, as an effective electronic descriptor that bridges interfacial friction and ferroelectric polarization across two-dimensional van der Waals multilayers, atomically thin films, and three-dimensional bulk ferroelectrics. ΔW is intrinsically correlated with the spin-polarized electronic structure near the Fermi level, and is intimately linked to both phonon-mediated energy dissipation and ferroelectric soft-mode dynamics. We demonstrate that the minimum-energy friction pathway coincides exactly with the ferroelectric switching trajectory. Along this pathway, sliding friction (f), ferroelectric polarization (P), and ΔW evolve synchronously, giving rise to robust linear scaling relationships: f ∝ ΔW and P ∝ ΔW. This scaling behavior persists regardless of orbital character, external pressure, finite temperature, or magnetic ordering effects. Our findings establish ΔW as a tunable quantum target for the concurrent optimization of ultralow friction and superior ferroelectric performance, paving the way for the rational design of energy-efficient interfacial systems and next-generation nanodevices.
title: Orbital weight variation as an effective electronic descriptor linking tribology and ferroelectric switching

abstract: The scale evolution of parton distributions is governed by splitting functions. We compute the four-loop splitting functions in perturbative QCD that control the evolution of quark nonsinglet distributions. We confirm previous partial results and obtain, for the first time, fully analytic expressions for all nonsinglet contributions at this order. These allow us to extract the analytic form of the four-loop virtual and rapidity anomalous dimensions entering logarithmic resummation. We provide precise numerical representations of the splitting functions suitable for parton evolution.
title: Four-Loop Nonsinglet Splitting Functions in QCD

abstract: In this Letter, we predict a structural phase transition unique to chiral crystals with screw symmetry. In chiral crystals, the phonon frequency renormalized by the electron-phonon coupling depends on the handedness of circular polarization. Consequently, the soft mode encoding phonon angular momentum induces spin-selective Peierls gaps in the electronic band, entailing a helical spin density wave and chiral lattice distortion. We also elucidate the chiral signatures and functional implications of collective modes. Our findings offer crucial insights into the emergence of chirality and highlight novel functional aspects of chiral materials and their design strategy.
title: Spontaneous spin-selective structural phase transition in chiral crystals

abstract: We report a search for the solar proton–proton ( p p ) neutrino flux via neutrino–electron elastic scattering using the PandaX-4T Run 2 data set collected between 2024 and 2026, corresponding to an exposure of 1.9 tonne ⋅ yr. Before Run 2 data taking, the detector underwent a series of upgrades to improve its response and background conditions. Time variations of radioactive noble-gas impurities are constrained using the physics data themselves, complemented by measurements from the gas-assay system. The analysis introduced improvements in the data processing chain, detector response characterization, and background models. A blind spectral analysis was then performed on the electronic-recoil data across a wide energy range from 20 to 1000 keV. In combination with the Run 0 data published earlier, the pp neutrino flux is derived to be ( 8.5 ± 3.5 ) × 10 10 c m − 2 s − 1 , consistent with the prediction of the Standard Solar Model. The combined dataset yields a 2.2 σ statistical significance for solar neutrino-electron scattering, representing the first positive indication obtained using data below the Borexino analysis threshold of 165~keV.
title: First Indication of Low-Energy Solar Neutrino-Electron Scattering with PandaX-4T Run 2 Data

abstract: Weak decays of charged kaons with an additional lepton-antilepton pair, K − → ℓ − ν ‾ ℓ ℓ ′ + ℓ ′ − ( K ℓ 2 ℓ ′ ), are suppressed at order $O(G_{F}^{2}\alpha_{\rm em}^{2})$ in the Standard Model (SM) and provide sensitive probes of its flavour structure, as well as independent determinations of the Cabibbo angle | V u s | . In this Letter we present the SM predictions for all four channels with ℓ , ℓ ′ = e , μ , based on the first complete lattice QCD calculation of the structure-dependent form factors reported in a companion paper [1]. Using the PDG value $|V_{us}|^{\rm PDG}=0.22431(85)$ , we obtain branching fractions with controlled uncertainties and precisions ranging from 2 % to 7 % , depending on the channel. For the three modes with published measurements, our results agree with experiment. For the K μ 2 μ mode, for which no published experimental result is available, we compare our prediction with the preliminary NA62 result, finding agreement at the 1.4 σ level. Conversely, the measured decay rates can be used together with our results to extract | V u s | from these modes. A weighted average over the two most precise channels, K μ 2 e and K μ 2 μ (the latter based on the preliminary NA62 result), yields | V u s | = 0.2283 ( 42 ) , corresponding to a 1.8 % determination. These results pave the way for using K ℓ 2 ℓ ′ decays as precision probes of the SM.
title: Rare kaon decays K − → ℓ − ν ‾ ℓ ℓ ′ + ℓ ′ − : Standard Model predictions from lattice QCD

abstract: We derive constraints on renormalization group (RG) flows and stability of phases in nonequilibrium systems using quantum information inequalities. These constraints involve conditional mutual information (CMI), which quantifies correlations between spatially separated regions not mediated by their surroundings. First, assuming CMI is UV finite, we derive a monotonicity constraint on its crossover scaling function. Under certain assumptions, this implies that the CMI scaling exponent cannot increase along the RG flow. Second, we bound the CMI of a convex mixture of states in terms of the CMI of individual components. We use this inequality to infer perturbative stability of spontaneous symmetry breaking states against quantum channels that explicitly break symmetry. We illustrate these constraints through several examples, including decoherence-driven transitions in classical symmetry-broken states, area-law CMI in anisotropic conserved dynamics, and even transitions in pure quantum states. We also discuss implications for classical nonequilibrium steady states.
title: Nonperturbative constraints on stability and renormalization group flows in nonequilibrium matter

abstract: The collective dynamics of spin textures driven by thermal fluctuations offer a path to understanding many-body thermodynamics in solid-state systems and designing high-dimensional probabilistic computing devices. However, due to the difficulty in experimental observation, quantitative modelling of this phenomenon remains elusive. Here, we report a direct measurement of spatial correlations between long-range fluctuating domain walls in ultra-weakly pinned ferrimagnetic thin films. The correlation can be dynamically tuned by extremely weak magnetic fields at sub-µT level. The results reveal an unprecedented linear decay in correlation with the DW distance. We precisely reconstruct the energy landscape that enables the quantification of experimental studies of correlation using the Edwards–Wilkinson equation. Our work provides a quantitative understanding of collective dynamics and can be useful for implementing energy-efficient spintronics devices.
title: Collective fluctuations of magnetic domain walls

abstract: Asymmetries of Autler-Townes doublets in resonant photoionization have recently attracted much attention. We show that antiresonances occurring after a field-induced avoided crossing are a novel source of pronounced asymmetry. The mechanism is distinct from the nonlinear dressed-atom stabilization effect recently revealed at extreme ultraviolet wavelengths, because it can arise for atoms that ionize exclusively from the excited state. The ionization rates of dressed states from Floquet theory are explained by an interferometric model. The effect is verified to persist for smooth pulse envelopes through simulations of the time-dependent Schrödinger equation for rubidium in 800 nm laser light. This opens up opportunities to control ionization in new parameter regimes of strong coupling, suitable for alkali atoms hybridized with laser light at optical and near infrared wavelengths.
title: Dressed-state stabilization through an antiresonance

abstract: The presence of free O–H groups at the water-air interface is essential for the uptake of gas molecules and surface chemical reactions, but their microscopic structure remains elusive. Combining polarization-resolved surface-specific spectroscopy with simulations, we unveil the heterogeneous structure of the free O-H group. Free O-H groups originate predominantly from well-structured water molecules that sit, on average, on the liquid side below the Gibbs dividing surface rather than from the more disordered molecules above the Gibbs dividing surface that protrude furthest into the vapor.
title: Two distinct types of free O-H groups at the water-air interface

abstract: We demonstrate that fluctuation-induced bistability is a robust and generic phenomenon in strongly interacting many-body systems with strong light-matter coupling. We identify a common microscopic mechanism based on resonances between photonic transitions and many-body energy scales, unifying the emergence of fluctuation-induced bistability for diverse types of matter, including interacting spins, fermions, and bosons coupled to cavity modes. We develop complementary methods to study both the steady-state properties of fluctuation-induced bistability and its dynamical formation at finite times. In particular, we introduce the dressed-state rate equation approach, which reveals rich metastable dynamics and enables the investigation of its system-size dependence. By comparing its predictions with numerically-exact tensor-network simulations, we identify signatures of fluctuation-induced bistability already in small systems on finite timescales. Our results show that fluctuation-induced bistability is not restricted to a specific statistics of the quantum matter and provide a framework for investigating its non-equilibrium dynamics across different cavity-coupled many-body quantum systems.
title: Fluctuation-induced bistability in the dissipative dynamics of generic cavity-matter quantum systems

abstract: We report the development and evaluation of a quantum logic spectroscopy based 25 Mg + − 27 Al + ion optical clock with a fractional systematic uncertainty of 4.8 × 10 − 19 . Multiple improvements are reported. The population leakage accumulation among Zeeman sublevels of the 25 Mg + ion hyperfine ground states during Raman sideband cooling is analyzed, enabling an optimal determination of the DC bias magnetic field. We also perform a direct measurement of the RF induced AC magnetic field in three directions. The quadratic Zeeman coefficient for the 1 S 0 ↔︎ 3 P 0 transition of 27 Al + ion is measured to be 𝐶 2 = −71.914(11) Hz/mT 2 . The quadratic Zeeman shift uncertainty is reduced by a factor of more than five without significant influence on the Raman sideband cooling of the ion pair. The three orthogonal Raman laser beam paths are optimized, enabling longer coherence time to suppress and evaluate the excess micromotion in three spatial directions. The demonstrated 27 Al + optical clock offers a reliable platform for future redefinition of the SI “second”.
title: 27 Al + ion optical clock with a fractional systematic uncertainty of 4.8 × 10 − 19

abstract: Optical excitation can generate excitons or carriers that interact with existing charge configurations to form new correlated phases. These states often exhibit nonequilibrium behavior and manifest phenomena such as interlayer excitonic insulator, Fermi-Bose mixed phases, magnetism, and even superconductivity. Here, we present signatures of electrically and optically induced hybrid-layer correlated states at both integer and fractional fillings in moiré heterostructures. Under an external electric field, the hybrid-layer correlated states can be interpreted as interlayer excitonic insulators at total fillings of 1/4, 1/3, 2/3, and 1. Near zero electric field, electrons from light-generated hot excitonic/electron-hole populations are trapped by the vacancy-like charge configurations in the moiré layer, while the remaining holes contribute to positive trion formation, manifesting a filling-selective nonequilibrium hybrid-layer response. Our results pave the way for the future exploration of complex interlayer correlated states.
title: Electrically and optically induced fractional hybrid-layer generalized Wigner crystals in moiré heterostructures

abstract: A limit on the permanent electric dipole moment (EDM) of the positive muon is presented based on data from the Fermilab Muon g − 2 Experiment taken between 2019 and 2020. The tracking detectors measure the average vertical decay angle of positrons from muon decays, enabling a search for an interaction between a possible muon EDM d μ and the lab-frame magnetic field. The result, d μ = ( − 0.35 ± 0.19 s t a t ± 0.34 s y s ) × 10 − 19 e ⋅ cm, is consistent with zero and sets a new direct limit on the muon EDM of | d μ | < 1.10 × 10 − 19 e ⋅ cm at the 95% confidence level.
title: Improved direct limit on the muon electric dipole moment

abstract: We present the first lattice QCD determination of the γ Z box contribution to parity-violating electron-proton scattering, ▫ γ Z , a key ingredient for the precise tests of the Standard Model via the proton weak charge. Our calculation covers the electron beam energies up to E = 155 MeV. At E = 0 , the vector contribution is known analytically and excluded by convention; for the remaining axial-vector component we obtain ▫ γ Z ( 0 ) = 0.00411 ( 9 ) . Incorporating this result implies a value for weak charge of Q W p = 0.06987 ( 50 ) . The calculated energy dependence of ▫ γ Z is directly relevant to the upcoming P2 experiment at Mainz, which will operate at the optimized beam energy of 155 MeV to extract Q W p . Although the systematic error budget in this exploratory study is not yet complete, this work establishes a lattice-QCD framework for computing the γ Z box contribution and demonstrates the feasibility of a first-principles approach, providing a foundation for future calculations with improved systematic control.
title: Lattice QCD determination of the γ Z box contribution to the proton weak charge

abstract: While cladding layers are essential for optical confinement in conventional waveguides, they limit spatial efficiency and integration density intrinsically. Recently, a cladding-free waveguide framework was proposed, in which each layer simultaneously serves as a signal-guiding core and an effective cladding for adjacent layers. However, existing photonic-crystal-based implementations involve complex three-dimensional architectures and additional metallic encapsulation, limiting further optimizations and on-chip integration. Here, we demonstrate a cladding-free plasmonic waveguide platform based on metasurface heterostructures with separated hyperbolic and elliptic equifrequency contours (EFCs). This approach harnesses the intrinsic subwavelength confinement of surface waves while maximizing spatial utilization. Crucially, the heterostructure interface supports an additional topologically protected edge state, characterized by high localization and singular field enhancement. Microwave experiments verify simultaneous, multiple-channel signal transmission and stable operation across a 90° bend. Our work significantly enhances the transmission channels of plasmonic waveguides, opening new avenues for on-chip photonic integration.
title: Cladding-free topological plasmonic waveguides in metasurface heterostructures
